articleHeadline: Deforestation increases the risk of leishmaniasis in the Amazon.
articleSummary: Deforestation in Acre, Brazilian Amazon, increases transmission risk for leishmaniasis and Chagas disease. articleHeadline: Mad Cow Disease: What It Is, How It Is Transmitted, and What the Risks to Humans Are.
articleSummary: Mad cow disease, formally bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), is a fatal neurodegenerative condition in cattle that gradually damages brain cells, altering movement and behavior. It has no cure. BSE is caused by prions, infectious protein particles without genetic material; when misfolded, they recruit other proteins and accumulate in the brain. Prions resist heat and standard sterilization, complicating decontamination. Transmission is believed to occur mainly through ingestion of contaminated feed containing prions from diseased animals, a mechanism highlighted during the 1990s United Kingdom outbreak. In humans, eating contaminated beef can cause variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (vCJD), a rare but fatal condition. Worldwide surveillance reports fewer than 250 vCJD cases; none have been reported in Brazil. Classic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in humans is predominantly sporadic (~85%), with ~15% hereditary; rare iatrogenic cases occur after exposure to contaminated human tissues. A recent human CJD case mentioned involving influencer Lito Sousa.
